changes: Content of the first reading kept as it was; only the notes are longer.
Notes now give another way to read the name: one compound name (Padmānanda-rāma, or 'Padma Ānandarāma'). They also note that the son_of relation depends on the doubtful final 'ja?'.
Notes now say the era is assumed to be VS because the script is Devanagari and the era is not named.

notes: The phrase 'padmā ānandarāmaja?' most likely means Padmā, son of Ānandarāma (ānandarāma-ja, 'born of Ānandarāma'). The cataloguer marked the final syllable as doubtful, so the son_of relation is uncertain. It is also possible that the whole string is one person's name, as the catalogue field 'Padmā Anandarāma ?' suggests; in that case there is a single scribe and no relation. 'Padmā' looks feminine, but '-ja' is masculine, so the true form may be Padma. The colophon does not name the era. VS is assumed because the script is Devanagari and the year is 1838; this gives about 1781 CE. Mārkaṇḍeya is left out because he is the mythical speaker of the stotra.
